title: Automation and Controls Engineer
description:
About Valar Atomics

At Valar Atomics, we're redefining what's possible in energy. Our mission is to make clean, high-temperature nuclear power scalable—unlocking abundant energy for industry, hydrogen, and next-generation manufacturing. We are a team of builders, engineers, and operators who believe nuclear energy should be fast to deploy, factory-made, and built for the real world. Our first pilot plant in Orangeville, Utah will demonstrate how advanced nuclear systems and fuel fabrication can power the future. Joining Valar Atomics means becoming part of a company where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level.

The Team

You will be joining Valar Atomics' Automation and Controls Team within the Instrumentation, Control & Electrical (IC&E) organization. I&C Software Engineers own the logic and data layer PLC and DCS application code, ISA-88 batch sequences, SCADA and HMI applications, historian infrastructure, and enterprise integration across the reactor program and fuel manufacturing operations. You will work alongside I&C Hardware, electrical, process, and nuclear safety engineers in an environment that blends traditional control systems with modern software and data integration practice. As an early-career engineer, you will be surrounded by senior, staff, and principal engineers whose job includes developing you. The team values operator-focused design, data integrity, disciplined documentation, and a safety-first culture.

The Role

Valar Atomics is seeking Automation and Controls Engineers to help develop, configure, test, and commission the control system software for our reactor and nuclear fuel manufacturing facilities. Working under the technical direction of senior and staff engineers, you will contribute across the controls software domain PLC programming, SCADA and HMI development, batch control, alarm configuration, historian work, and control system testing, with steadily increasing independence and ownership. This is an early-career position built for growth: you will write real application code that runs a real plant, spend time at panels and in the field during loop checks and commissioning, have your work reviewed and tested by experienced engineers, and learn nuclear-grade software discipline on a first-of-a-kind reactor program. We expect engineers at this level to develop toward independent ownership of controls software scope within their first few years.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and modify PLC and DCS application code on platforms such as Rockwell ControlLogix/CompactLogix, Siemens S7/TIA Portal, or equivalent, using IEC 61131-3 languages, working within established coding standards and template libraries and with structured code review by senior engineers.
  • Build and maintain SCADA application content on platforms such as Ignition, FactoryTalk, AVEVA, or WinCC — tag databases, user-defined types, display instances, and scripting — from established templates and standards.
  • Develop HMI displays at the panel and supervisory levels in accordance with the team's ISA-101/HPHMI style guide, including navigation, faceplates, and situational awareness graphics, with displays reviewed before release.
  • Implement ISA-88 batch phase logic and equipment module code within the established batch architecture, under the direction of senior engineers; support recipe configuration and batch testing.
  • Configure alarm setpoints, priorities, deadbands, and shelving in accordance with the approved alarm philosophy and rationalization outputs; run alarm performance KPI reports.
  • Support safety logic work under IEC 61511 by executing functional test procedures, documenting test results, and assisting with safety application code under direct senior engineer supervision; safety logic authorship and approval remain with senior engineers.
  • Configure historian tags, compression and exception settings, and asset framework elements within the established model; build process data dashboards and operational reports.
  • Configure and troubleshoot industrial communication interfaces including OPC-UA, EtherNet/IP, and Modbus TCP/RTU under guidance — server and client endpoints, tag mapping, and SCADA-to-PLC connections.
  • Write SQL queries and Python scripts for data processing, report generation, and control system test automation.
  • Apply the team's software configuration management practice: version control, change control, structured code review participation, and controller and SCADA application backup and restore.
  • Execute software FAT, SAT, and commissioning test procedures; support loop checks and end-to-end testing with I&C Hardware engineers; document results and maintain tag lists, alarm databases, and as-built software records.
  • Troubleshoot control system software faults including communication failures, logic defects, sequence stalls, and historian data gaps, escalating appropriately and documenting findings and corrective actions.
  • Support coordination with I&C Hardware Engineers on I/O assignment, tag naming, signal scaling, and loop commissioning.
  • Maintain disciplined engineering records consistent with nuclear quality requirements, ensuring traceability of design decisions, software changes, and test results.
  • Actively develop technical competence through structured learning, commissioning time, and progressively larger assignments, in line with the team's engineer development expectations.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Electronic, Computer, Systems Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
  • 2+ years of experience in controls software, PLC programming, SCADA development, or related automation work; substantial internship or co-op experience may be counted toward this at the hiring manager's discretion.
  • Hands-on PLC programming experience with at least one major platform (Rockwell, Siemens, or equivalent) using one or more IEC 61131-3 languages.
  • Some hands-on exposure to SCADA or HMI development on a major platform (Ignition, FactoryTalk, AVEVA, WinCC, or equivalent).
  • Ability to read and interpret P&IDs, loop diagrams, and I/O lists sufficient to develop and test control logic.
  • Basic familiarity with at least one industrial communication protocol (OPC-UA, EtherNet/IP, or Modbus).
  • Working familiarity with version control concepts and disciplined change practice for application code.
  • Willingness and ability to work hands-on during loop checks, commissioning, and plant support, including at times in industrial conditions and on commissioning schedules.
  • Strong documentation habits and attention to detail, and willingness to work within a rigorous nuclear quality and checking culture.
  • Ability to take direction, incorporate code review comments constructively, and communicate status and problems clearly.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Platform certification such as Ignition (Core/Gold) or Rockwell/Siemens training credentials.
  • Engineer in Training (EIT) designation or passage of the FE exam.
  • Internship, co-op, or work experience in process industries, manufacturing, utilities, or system integration.
  • Exposure to batch control (ISA-88), alarm management (ISA-18.2), or HMI design (ISA-101) concepts.
  • Exposure to plant historians (PI, Ignition Historian, or equivalent) or operational dashboarding.
  • Exposure to safety system logic or functional safety testing concepts (IEC 61511).
  • Experience with SQL, Python, or REST APIs for data processing or integration.
  • Experience with Git or equivalent version control.
  • Personal, academic, or professional projects demonstrating hands-on controls, automation, or software work.

What We Offer

  • Competitive base salary
  • Equity ownership in a rapidly growing advanced energy company
  • Comprehensive medical benefits
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Free daily lunch and dinner provided onsite
  • Generous PPE stipend
  • High-impact startup environment with significant ownership and autonomy
  • Opportunities for rapid career growth and internal advancement
  • Direct collaboration with experienced operators, engineers, and industry leaders
  • The opportunity to help build and scale transformative energy technology from the ground up

description:
About Valar Atomics

The Role

Our HTGR power conversion system will be built around a secondary loop Brayton cycle, high-speed turbomachinery operating on helium, sCO2, and even air at extreme temperatures and pressures, paired with development generator sets and a purpose-built test facility program. The Director of IC&E for Power Conversion owns the full instrumentation, control, and electrical architecture across this system: from early R&D and rig design through test facility construction, commissioning, and ultimately integrated plant operation.

This role demands someone who can operate at two levels simultaneously with a hands-on technical authority who understands turbomachinery dynamics, high-speed generator control, and test system instrumentation at a deep level, and a team leader who builds and develops the IC&E organization around the power conversion program. Candidates from oil & gas, aerospace propulsion, industrial turbomachinery, or power generation are strongly preferred. Nuclear background is a plus, not a prerequisite.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Leadership — Turbomachinery & Power Conversion

  • Own the IC&E design basis for the primary to secondary coolant loop Brayton cycle power conversion unit (PCU), including compressor, turbine, recuperator, and intercooler control systems
  • Define instrumentation strategy for high-speed rotating machinery — shaft dynamics, vibration monitoring, tip clearance, temperature, pressure, and flow measurement in helium environments
  • Develop control system architecture for turbomachinery startup, shutdown, load following, trip logic, and speed/load governing
  • Lead IC&E design for development generator sets — excitation systems, voltage regulation, synchronization, protection relays, and grid interface or islanded operation schemes
  • Establish electrical power distribution design for the power conversion facility: MV/LV switchgear, variable frequency drives (VFDs), power electronics, and auxiliary systems

Test Facility Design, Construction & Commissioning

  • Lead IC&E scope for the design and construction of turbomachinery development and test facilities — from instrumentation layout and data acquisition architecture through facility electrical design
  • Own IC&E commissioning planning and execution
  • Establish instrumentation calibration programs, measurement uncertainty budgets, and data quality standards for development testing

Program & Team Leadership

  • Build, lead, and mentor the power conversion IC&E engineering team across disciplines, controls, instrumentation, electrical, and data systems
  • Define team structure, staffing plans, and competency roadmap as the program scales from R&D through construction and commissioning phases
  • Manage IC&E scope, schedule, and budget within the broader power conversion program
  • Select and manage IC&E vendors, system integrators, and instrumentation suppliers; define qualification, calibration, and acceptance requirements
  • Collaborate closely with turbomachinery, mechanical, thermal-hydraulics, systems engineering, and the reactor IC&E team to ensure integrated plant control architecture is coherent across the PCU–reactor interface

Phase Continuity

  • Carry IC&E ownership across all power conversion program phases: conceptual design → detailed engineering → test facility procurement and construction → commissioning and integrated testing → reactor plant integration

You Will Be Successful in This Role If

  • You enjoy solving first-of-a-kind engineering challenges where there is no existing playbook

Basic Qualifications

  • Experience leading IC&E scope on test facilities, development rigs, or capital construction projects
  • Strong foundation in electrical systems design: switchgear, motor drives, protection and controls, and facility power distribution
  • Experience managing IC&E teams and vendor relationships across multiple project phases

Preferred Skills and Experience

description:
About Valar Atomics

The Team

The ModSim Engineering Group is a dynamic analysis and engineering group that provides the analytical foundation for reactor and plant design, delivering high-fidelity computational analysis, integrated directly into the engineering design process.

The group responsibilities spans:

  • Neutronics and reactor design;
  • Thermal-hydraulics systems analysis covering steady-state and transient performance of the complete system; and
  • Computational fluid dynamics and finite element analysis for detailed flow, thermal, and structural integrity assessment.

ModSim works alongside the engineering and licensing organizations and develops and maintains the models that underpin design basis definition, transient and accident analysis, safety case development and regulatory submittals, applying rigorous verification, validation and uncertainty quantification throughout. The group's responsibilities extend beyond prediction: models are benchmarked against test data and against operating data from research and demonstration reactors in construction and service, closing the loop between simulation, as-built plant performance, and the continuous improvement of the company's analytical methods and business case.

The Role

The Director of ModSim leads VALAR Atomics’ modeling, simulation, and analysis organization across CFD, FEA, thermal-hydraulics, and nuclear engineering, and is accountable for ensuring that analysis supports the design process and outputs that get built.

Reporting to the CNO / VP of Engineering, the Director of ModSim owns the strategy, quality, throughput, resourcing, and budget of the group; the multiphysics integration and verification-and-validation (V&V) consistency that bind the disciplines together; and the licensing-grade defensibility of every deliverable under a nuclear quality program (i.e. NQA-1, 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, ASME V&V 10/20/30).

In a dynamic, speed-driven start-up racing to deploy reactors at scale, the ModSim Director is equal parts technical authority, org-builder, systems thinker, and dot-connector, growing the team from a small core, automating the simulation-to-design workflow, and wiring ModSim into design, manufacturing, licensing, and construction so that models become steel, on schedule and to code. This is a hands-on-enough leader who is as comfortable interrogating a Flownex transient or a neutronics depletion run as standing on a fabrication floor asking why the as-built diverges from the model.

Key Responsibilities

The Director carries seven areas of accountability, spanning technical leadership, people, integration, reporting, and relentless optimization of output rate, speed, and quality:

  • Technical leadership across the four core disciplines. Set the analysis strategy, methods, and standards for CFD, FEA, thermal-hydraulics, and neutronics; own multiphysics integration, cross-discipline data-exchange conventions, configuration control, and end-to-end V&V so the coupled picture is consistent and defensible.
  • Close the loop from model to build hardware. Ensure analysis directly supports design outputs, i.e., sized components, qualified structures, validated systems, and stays connected through procurement, fabrication, construction, and commissioning; drive validation and design-for-manufacture feedback so the digital model and the physical plant stay in alignment.
  • Build, grow, and develop the team. Recruit, mentor and retain Stream/Discipline Leads and their analysts; scale a small start-up core into a high-performing multidisciplinary group; engage SMEs and external partners; create the culture, career paths and technical bar for the organization.
  • Integrate ModSim within the wider engineering enterprise. Partner with design, systems engineering, manufacturing, licensing/safety, project management, and construction so that simulation is embedded in the design process rather than bolted on; make ModSim the trusted, single source of analytical truth across groups.
  • Report to and advise executive leadership. Serve as the senior simulation interface to the CNO / VP of Engineering and executive team; translate complex analysis into clear, decision-grade guidance on risk, schedule, cost, and design choices.
  • Relentlessly optimize output rate and quality. Drive throughput and rigor together via workflow automation, scripting, templated and parametric models, digital-thread / digital-engineering tooling, HPC scaling, and reusable V&V, etc., so the group delivers more, faster, without compromising nuclear-grade quality.
  • Own quality, licensing-readiness, tooling, and budget. Hold accountability for the nuclear QA and V&V framework (NQA-1, 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, ASME V&V 10/20/30) and licensing-grade defensibility (NRC 10 CFR Part 50/52/53, ASME codes); manage the simulation software portfolio, HPC resources, vendor relationships and group

Basic Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in engineering (MSc/MEng), or equivalent work experience required — Nuclear, Mechanical, Aerospace, or a closely related discipline; PhD strongly preferred.
  • 15+ years in engineering simulation and analysis, with substantial multidisciplinary leadership and team / program management (a strong 10+-year track record with exceptional build-to-deployment credentials will be considered).
  • Demonstrated experience taking modeling and analysis through to design, constructed and/or operating hardware – not solely paper studies.
  • Depth in at least one of CFD, FEA, thermal-hydraulics or neutronics, with the breadth to direct and critically review the others.
  • Experience working under a formal quality program (NQA-1, ISO 9001, 10 CFR 50 Appendix B or equivalent) and within a regulated environment (NRC, ASME, or comparable such as naval nuclear, aerospace/FAA, or DoD).
  • S. Person status (or ability to meet U.S. nuclear export-control requirements under 10 CFR Part 810 / ITAR-EAR) and ability to obtain any required DOE/NRC access or clearance.

Preferred Skills and Experience

A strong candidate will bring most of the following – the blend of computational depth, engineering breadth, and delivery credibility this role demands:

Simulation & computational engineering

  • Hands-on mastery of one or more of: Ansys Fluent/CFX (CFD), Ansys Mechanical (FEA), Flownex SE, RELAP5-3D, TRACE, and/or MELCOR (thermal-hydraulic systems), and neutronics tools (OpenMC, SCALE, Serpent, MCNP); ability to direct and review all four.
  • Multiphysics coupling, verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification (ASME V&V 10/20/30); model configuration control and traceability.
  • Systems engineering and digital engineering / digital-thread practice; workflow automation and scripting (Python, APIs, journaling) and parametric / templated modeling; HPC at scale.

Engineering & domain breadth

  • Engineering design and the design-to-build lifecycle: design-for-manufacture, tolerancing, procurement, fabrication, construction support and commissioning.
  • Thermal-hydraulics and heat transfer; turbomachinery; heat exchangers; high-pressure piping (ASME B31, Section III); control and dynamics / transient plant behavior.
  • Nuclear reactor design (HTGR / gas-cooled experience a major plus: helium coolant, TRISO fuel, graphite core, high-temperature materials, Brayton / supercritical-CO₂ power conversion, process-heat applications).
  • Manufacturing and construction realities – what it actually takes to fabricate, weld, inspect, assemble and integrate a plant.

Quality, licensing & delivery

  • Nuclear quality assurance (NQA-1, 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, ISO 9001) and software QA.
  • Nuclear licensing and safety (NRC 10 CFR Part 50/52/53), ASME code application (Section III, VIII, B31), and interaction with regulators and external reviewers.

You will work alongside I&C, mechanical, and nuclear safety engineers in a collaborative environment that demands technical precision and a strong safety culture, with the opportunity to contribute to some of the most technically interesting power distribution challenges in the advanced nuclear sector.

The Role

Valar Atomics is seeking an Electrical Engineer to support the design and delivery of MV/LV electrical systems for nuclear fuel manufacturing facilities. The role will contribute to electrical system design, power system studies, equipment selection, drawings, specifications, and field support while working closely with senior electrical engineers and multidisciplinary teams. This is an opportunity to work on first-of-a-kind industrial facilities and develop hands-on experience with complex electrical systems in the nuclear industry.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain electrical load lists and support power system studies including load flow, short circuit, voltage drop, motor starting, and harmonic analysis using SKM Power Tools, ETAP, or equivalent.
  • Prepare arc flash hazard analysis in accordance with IEEE 1584 and substation grounding calculations in accordance with IEEE 80.
  • Assist with sizing and selection of transformers, cables, switchgear, bus systems, capacitor banks, UPS systems, and batteries.
  • Develop and update single line diagrams for MV and LV distribution systems from the utility interface through MCCs and final distribution equipment.
  • Prepare and maintain electrical equipment layouts, cable schedules, tray routing, and underground duct bank designs.
  • Support specifications and data sheets for MV switchgear, LV switchboards, MCCs, distribution panelboards, transformers, bus ducts, VFDs, UPS systems, and standby generators.
  • Support electrical area classification drawings and selection of equipment for hazardous areas in accordance with NEC/CEC 500 or IEC 60079 series.

The I&C Specialist is the bridge between engineering design and working plant hardware, leading commissioning, owning calibration and field troubleshooting, and supervising the technicians who install and maintain the instrumentation. You will work alongside I&C Hardware and Software Engineers, process and mechanical engineers, operations, and nuclear safety in an environment where field execution quality directly supports production reliability and nuclear safety. The team values hands-on expertise, disciplined documentation, and a safety-first culture.

The Role

Valar Atomics is seeking an Instrumentation & Controls Specialist to serve as the site's hands-on expert in instrumentation and control hardware for nuclear fuel manufacturing facilities. This is a field-focused role centered on instrument installation, calibration, configuration, and troubleshooting, with primary responsibility for planning, leading, and executing commissioning activities and for supervising the I&C technician group. The position suits an experienced technical specialist who wants ownership of field execution without moving into a design engineering role.

Key Responsibilities

  • Install, calibrate, configure, troubleshoot, and maintain field instrumentation including flow, pressure, differential pressure, temperature, level, and analytical devices, using manufacturer procedures and site standards.
  • Calibrate and maintain final control elements including control valves, actuators, positioners, and regulators; perform bench and in-situ calibration, stroke and response testing, packing and seat maintenance, and valve signature analysis.
  • Plan, lead, and execute commissioning activities including commissioning schedule development and sequencing, preparation of loop check and functional test packages, coordination of craft and vendor resources, punch list management, and system turnover to operations.
  • Execute and document loop checks, point-to-point continuity checks, calibration verification, and end-to-end interlock testing from sensor through final element; drive punch list items to closure.
  • Supervise the I&C technician group including daily work assignment, verification of task qualification and training records, on-the-job training and sign-off, and performance input to I&C leadership.
  • Own execution of the instrument calibration program including calibration scheduling and recall, management of standards and test equipment, traceability to NIST-referenced standards, and integrity of calibration records.
  • Configure and troubleshoot smart field devices using HART communicators and instrument asset management software; manage device descriptor files, ranging, damping, and diagnostic alarm configuration.
  • Terminate and troubleshoot field wiring, panel terminations, and I/O connections; diagnose grounding, shielding, and noise-induced signal problems; verify intrinsic safety installations against entity parameters.
  • Install and commission instrumentation in classified hazardous areas in accordance with NEC Article 500/505 or IEC 60079 and applicable installation and work permits.
  • Execute safety instrumented system field work including proof testing and documentation, bypass control, and safety device replacement under approved procedures.
  • Support control loop tuning and plant startup, working with I&C Engineering to resolve measurement quality, final element response, and loop performance issues.
  • Red-line and maintain field documentation including loop diagrams, hook-up drawings, instrument index entries, panel and wiring drawings, and as-built mark-ups; route changes through the engineering document control process.

  • Write and review I&C work packages and job hazard analyses; enforce lockout/tagout, hot work, confined space, radiological work practice, and foreign material exclusion requirements for all I&C field work.
  • Provide field feedback to I&C Engineering on instrument selection, installation detail, accessibility, and maintainability for new and modified installations.
  • Direct contractor and vendor field crews on I&C installation and commissioning scope; verify workmanship against project standards and nuclear quality requirements before acceptance.

Equivalent hands-on I&C experience will be considered in lieu of a formal credential. A four-year degree is not required.
  • Minimum 7+ years of hands-on I&C experience in process, chemical, power, or nuclear facilities.
  • Demonstrated experience planning and leading commissioning activities including loop checking, functional testing, punch list closure, and system turnover.
  • Expert-level ability to calibrate, configure, and troubleshoot field instrumentation across flow, pressure, temperature, level, and analytical measurement.
  • Experience calibrating and maintaining control valves, actuators, and positioners.
  • Ability to read and interpret P&IDs, loop diagrams, hook-up drawings, panel and wiring schematics, and instrument data sheets.
  • Proficiency with HART communicators, calibration equipment, pressure and temperature standards, and electrical test instruments.
  • Experience with field wiring and termination practice including grounding, shielding, and signal segregation.
  • Working knowledge of hazardous area installation requirements (NEC Article 500/505 or IEC 60079) and intrinsic safety practice.
  • Experience supervising or directing technicians or contractor craft crews.
  • Ability to work at heights, in confined spaces, and while wearing personal protective equipment including respiratory protection as required.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • ISA Certified Control Systems Technician (CCST) Level II or Level III.
  • Journeyman electrician license or state instrumentation certification.
  • Experience with instrument asset management systems (Emerson AMS, Siemens PDM, Honeywell FDM, or equivalent).
  • Experience with analytical instrumentation such as gas analyzers, mass spectrometry, moisture analyzers, pH, and conductivity measurement.
  • Experience with radiation monitoring instrumentation, criticality monitoring, or nuclear-qualified instrumentation.
  • Experience in nuclear, DOE, or NRC-regulated facilities working under NQA-1 or 10 CFR 50 Appendix B quality programs.
  • Experience with instrument work in cleanroom, glovebox, or contamination-controlled environments.
  • Experience executing safety instrumented system proof tests and associated IEC 61511 documentation.
  • Experience with instrumentation in corrosive, high-purity, high-temperature, or molten salt service.
  • Working familiarity with PLC and SCADA systems (Rockwell, Siemens, Ignition, or equivalent) sufficient to verify I/O status and trace signals during troubleshooting.
  • Experience with CMMS or work order systems (Maximo, SAP PM, Fiix, or equivalent).
  • Experience writing commissioning plans, test procedures, or maintenance procedures.

title: Lead Electrical Engineer
description:
About Valar Atomics

At Valar Atomics, we're redefining what's possible in energy. Our mission is to make clean, high-temperature nuclear power scalable—unlocking abundant energy for industry, hydrogen, and next-generation manufacturing. We are a team of builders, engineers, and operators who believe nuclear energy should be fast to deploy, factory-made, and built for the real world. Our first pilot plant in Orangeville, Utah will demonstrate how advanced nuclear systems and fuel fabrication can power the future. Joining Valar Atomics means becoming part of a company where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level.

The Team

You will lead Valar Atomics' Electrical Engineering team within the Instrumentation, Control & Electrical (IC&E) organization. The team delivers the electrical infrastructure that powers and is powered by Valar's facilities, from utility and grid interconnection through generation, MV distribution, process area LV systems, and emergency power across the reactor program, fuel manufacturing operations, and power generation and distribution scope. You will work alongside I&C, mechanical, process, power conversion, and nuclear safety engineers in a hands-on environment where power system integrity directly supports production reliability and nuclear safety, with some of the most technically interesting generation and distribution challenges in the advanced nuclear sector. The team values technical depth, disciplined documentation, and a safety-first culture, and you will set that tone for the engineers you hire.

The Role

Valar Atomics is seeking a Lead Electrical Engineer to lead and build our electrical engineering team, and to own electrical engineering delivery across the full plant scope, Reactor, Nuclear Fuel Manufacturing, Power Generation, and Power Distribution. This is a player-coach role: you will be both the team's leader, hiring, developing, directing, and growing electrical engineers across our career ladder, and its most senior technical voice while that team is built, with design responsibility spanning LV, MV, and HV systems from utility interconnection and the generation switchyard through medium voltage distribution to process and facility low voltage systems. You will own the electrical architecture of a first-of-a-kind nuclear power plant, including its power generation electrical scope: generator integration, excitation and protection, step-up transformation, and grid interconnection. This role builds the organization it will lead.

Key Responsibilities

Team Leadership and Organization Building

  • Build the electrical engineering team: define roles and requisitions across the Engineer / Senior / Staff / Principal ladder with the Director, recruit and interview candidates, own hiring recommendations, and onboard and integrate new engineers.
  • Lead the team day to day: assign and prioritize work across the four plant areas, direct and review technical output, manage performance, and develop each engineer's technical depth and progression along the ladder.
  • Own engineering resourcing strategy: workload forecasting across Reactor, Nuclear Fuel Manufacturing, Power Generation, and Power Distribution scopes; internal versus contractor engineering allocation; and technical direction and oversight of engineering subcontractors and consultants.
  • Establish the discipline's ways of working — checking practice, calculation and study bases, design standards, and documentation discipline — and evolve their ownership to Staff and Principal engineers as the team grows.

Technical Leadership and Delivery

  • Own electrical engineering delivery across all four plant areas: the scope, quality, and schedule of power system studies, designs, specifications, and construction and commissioning support produced by the team.
  • Own the plant electrical architecture end-to-end across voltage classes: HV utility interconnection and switchyard, generator and generator step-up (GSU) transformer integration, MV distribution, LV process and facility systems, emergency and standby power, and DC/UPS systems.
  • Own the power generation electrical scope: generator specification and integration with the power conversion system, excitation and voltage regulation, generator and interconnection protection, synchronization, auxiliary power, and grid code and interconnection technical requirements.
  • Serve as the discipline's senior technical authority: approve power system studies (load flow, short circuit, arc flash, protection coordination, grounding), one-line development, protection philosophy and relay settings, and major equipment specifications, delegating approval authority to Staff and Principal engineers as they are hired.
  • Own the utility and AHJ technical relationships: interconnection studies and agreements, protection interface requirements, code interpretation and compliance strategy, and inspection support.
  • Lead the electrical discipline in interdisciplinary design reviews, HAZOP studies, and licensing-support activities; represent the discipline's position at program level and own resolution of cross-discipline conflicts.
  • Lead vendor engagement for major electrical packages: pre-qualification, technical bid evaluation, award recommendation, factory acceptance activities, and escalation of systemic vendor issues.

Program Coordination

  • Coordinate electrical scope and interfaces across the reactor, fuel manufacturing, power conversion, and site infrastructure programs, including load growth, sequencing of energisation, and shared distribution infrastructure decisions.
  • Advise IC&E leadership on electrical technical risk, resourcing, and sequencing; provide independent technical judgment where schedule and cost pressure intersect engineering integrity.
  • Maintain disciplined engineering records consistent with nuclear quality requirements, ensuring traceability of design decisions, analyses, and test results, and setting the example for the team's documentation culture.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a closely related discipline.
  • 10+ years of electrical engineering experience across power generation, utility, process, or industrial projects.
  • Demonstrated experience leading an electrical engineering team: assigning and directing work, reviewing and approving other engineers' output, and developing engineers — not solely project or matrix leadership.
  • Experience building an engineering team through direct hiring: defining roles, recruiting, interviewing, and onboarding engineers you then led.
  • Substantial power generation electrical experience, including generator integration, excitation, generator and interconnection protection, GSU transformers, switchyard or substation scope, and grid interconnection requirements. Experience from cogeneration / combined heat and power (CHP) facilities fully satisfies this requirement.
  • Demonstrated design proficiency across LV, MV, and HV systems — from utility/transmission-level interconnection and switchyards through MV distribution to LV process and facility systems, including the studies, protection, and equipment specification appropriate to each voltage class.
  • Expert-level proficiency in power system analysis (SKM Power Tools, ETAP, PSS/E, or equivalent), including ownership or approval of load flow, short circuit, arc flash, and protection coordination studies.
  • Demonstrated end-to-end ownership of electrical scope on at least one major capital project, from front-end design through energisation and commissioning.
  • Strong working knowledge of applicable codes and standards (NEC/NFPA 70, IEEE including the C37 protection series, NEMA, ANSI, IEC), sufficient to set and defend discipline standards.
  • Experience representing an electrical discipline to external parties — utilities, AHJs, regulators, or major vendors.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Professional Engineer (P.E. / P.Eng.) registration or equivalent.
  • Experience leading utility interconnection from application through energisation, including interconnection agreements and PPA technical interfaces.
  • Nuclear facility electrical experience, including nuclear classification and separation requirements (IEEE 384, Class 1E concepts) or work under NQA-1 / 10 CFR 50 Appendix B quality programs.
  • Generator protection expertise (IEEE C37.102) and experience with synchronization, black start, or islanded operation schemes.
  • Experience with IEC 61850 substation automation and protection communication.
  • Experience with emergency and standby power system design, DC systems, and battery sizing (IEEE 485/1115).
  • Experience on first-of-a-kind, prototype, or early-stage plant programs where the electrical organization and its standards had to be built rather than inherited.

What We Offer

  • Competitive base salary
  • Equity ownership in a rapidly growing advanced energy company
  • Comprehensive medical benefits
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Free daily lunch and dinner provided onsite
  • Generous PPE stipend
  • High-impact startup environment with significant ownership and autonomy
  • Opportunities for rapid career growth and internal advancement
  • Direct collaboration with experienced operators, engineers, and industry leaders

title: Principal Instrumentation & Controls Engineer – Hardware
description:
About Valar Atomics

At Valar Atomics, we're redefining what's possible in energy. Our mission is to make clean, high-temperature nuclear power scalable—unlocking abundant energy for industry, hydrogen, and next-generation manufacturing. We are a team of builders, engineers, and operators who believe nuclear energy should be fast to deploy, factory-made, and built for the real world. Our first pilot plant in Orangeville, Utah will demonstrate how advanced nuclear systems and fuel fabrication can power the future. Joining Valar Atomics means becoming part of a company where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level.

The Team

You will be joining Valar Atomics' Instrumentation, Control & Electrical (IC&E) organization. I&C Hardware Engineers own the physical measurement and control layer field instrumentation and final elements, control panels and I/O architecture, field wiring and network infrastructure, and safety instrumented system hardware, along with the calibration and commissioning practices that keep those systems trustworthy. You will work alongside I&C software, process, electrical, mechanical, and nuclear safety engineers in a hands-on environment where measurement quality and installation integrity directly support production reliability and nuclear safety. As the principal engineer, you will be the discipline's most senior technical voice: the architect of its systems, the final checker of its highest-consequence work, and a standard-setter for the engineers who will build their careers here. The team values technical depth, disciplined documentation, and a safety-first culture.

The Role

Valar Atomics is seeking Principal Instrumentation & Controls Hardware Engineers to own the technical direction of the instrumentation and control hardware discipline across our reactor and nuclear fuel manufacturing facilities. The role spans the full instrumentation hardware domain: field instruments and final elements, control panel and I/O architecture, hazardous area design, safety instrumented system hardware, field wiring and OT network infrastructure, and calibration and commissioning practice, but at the level of architecture, strategy, and design authority rather than routine execution. This is a principal position: you will define the measurement and control hardware architecture and technology roadmap for a first-of-a-kind nuclear program, hold final technical approval authority within the discipline, direct the resolution of the highest-consequence and most novel engineering problems, represent the discipline to regulators, standards bodies, and strategic vendors, and build the engineering capability of the organization around you. Where a Staff engineer owns the discipline's standards and quality, the Principal engineer owns where the discipline is going.

Key Responsibilities

Architecture and Technical Strategy

  • Define and own the I&C hardware architecture and technology roadmap across the reactor program and fuel manufacturing facilities, including instrument platform and protocol strategy, panel and I/O architecture philosophy, safety instrumented system architecture philosophy, and OT network physical infrastructure strategy.
  • Author and own the discipline's design philosophy and basis documents, measurement strategy, redundancy and segregation philosophy, hazardous area design approach, grounding and shielding philosophy, and calibration and maintenance philosophy that constrain and guide all downstream project engineering.
  • Direct measurement technology strategy for first-of-a-kind and severe-service conditions where no proven commercial solution exists, including sponsoring technology trade studies, vendor development programs, prototype and qualification campaigns, and make-or-buy decisions with long-term consequences.
  • Own the discipline's standards program: set the framework and priorities for engineering standards, delegate authorship to staff and senior engineers, and approve standards for release; drive convergence and standardization across projects and sites.
  • Evaluate emerging instrumentation, diagnostics, and OT infrastructure technology; decide what enters the toolkit, what is piloted, and what is excluded, balancing innovation against nuclear quality and long-term supportability.

Design Authority and Technical Governance

  • Serve as the discipline design authority: hold final technical approval within I&C hardware for architecture decisions, safety-significant designs, deviations from standards, and concessions; adjudicate technical disputes within the discipline and represent its position in cross-discipline conflicts at program level.
  • Own the technical integrity of safety instrumented system hardware across the fleet, including SIS architecture selection, redundancy and voting philosophy, SIL verification methodology, and approval of safety-significant SIS design changes in accordance with IEC 61511 and IEC 61508.
  • Lead the discipline's engagement in the highest-consequence program reviews: preliminary and critical design reviews, safety case and licensing reviews, HAZOP/LOPA at program level, and readiness reviews for major commissioning and startup milestones.
  • Direct root cause investigations for the most significant failures and events touching instrumentation hardware; approve corrective action strategy and ensure findings are institutionalized in architecture, standards, and training.
  • Personally execute or lead engineering on the small set of problems where the consequence of error or the degree of novelty warrants the discipline's most senior engineer and know which problems those are.

External Representation and Licensing

  • Support the nuclear licensing effort as the senior instrumentation hardware voice: contribute to and defend the instrumentation and SIS content of the safety case, support regulatory interactions and audits, and shape the licensing basis so it remains buildable and operable.
  • Represent Valar Atomics to strategic instrumentation vendors and technology partners at a senior technical level; own long-term vendor technical relationships, qualification expectations, and escalation of systemic vendor quality issues.
  • Represent the company in industry and standards forums as appropriate (ISA, IEEE, IEC, advanced reactor industry groups); bring emerging regulatory and standards developments back into company strategy before they become constraints.

Organizational Capability

  • Build the discipline's engineering capability: define the technical competencies the organization needs, shape role definitions and the technical career ladder with the Director, set the hiring bar, and lead technical interviews for senior positions.
  • Mentor staff and senior engineers toward independent technical authority; sponsor their development through delegation of ownership with oversight rather than retention of scope.
  • Advise IC&E leadership on technical risk, resourcing, and sequencing for the program; provide independent technical judgment on schedule and cost pressure where it intersects engineering integrity.
  • Maintain disciplined engineering records consistent with nuclear quality requirements, ensuring traceability of design decisions, analyses, and test results, and setting the example for the discipline's documentation culture.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Electronic, Mechanical, Chemical, or Systems Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • 10+ years of instrumentation or I&C engineering experience in process industries.
  • Demonstrated end-to-end ownership of instrumentation hardware scope across multiple major capital projects, including at least one taken from concept or front-end design through commissioning, startup, and initial operations.
  • Track record of architecture-level technical leadership: defining instrumentation or SIS architecture, design philosophy, or engineering standards that were adopted across an organization or program, not just a single project.
  • Recognized technical authority in at least one deep area of the discipline (for example: severe-service measurement, SIS engineering, hazardous area design, or large-scale instrumentation infrastructure), evidenced by design authority roles, published work, standards participation, or a verifiable internal reputation as the final technical reference.
  • Deep, hands-on command of the full instrumentation hardware domain: instrument and valve selection and sizing, panel and I/O architecture, hazardous area classification (NEC 500/505 or IEC 60079), field wiring, grounding and shielding practice, calibration, and loop commissioning.
  • Substantial safety instrumented system experience across the IEC 61511 lifecycle, including architecture selection, SIL verification, and approval or checking authority over SIS deliverables.
  • Experience directing and developing other engineers, including senior-level engineers, and reviewing and approving their work as a formal checker or design authority.
  • Experience representing an engineering discipline to external parties — regulators, certification bodies, major vendors, or client design authorities.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Professional Engineer (PE) license.
  • ISA Certified Automation Professional (CAP) or ISA84 Safety Instrumented Systems expert credential, or equivalent.
  • Nuclear industry experience, including 10 CFR 50 Appendix B / NQA-1 quality programs, nuclear-qualified instrumentation, radiation and criticality monitoring, or instrumentation content of a nuclear safety case.
  • Experience selecting, developing, or qualifying instrumentation for novel or severe service high-temperature, high-pressure gas, corrosive, high-purity, or molten salt, including first-of-a-kind qualification programs.
  • Experience on first-of-a-kind or prototype plants where instrumentation strategy had to be developed without established precedent.
  • Participation in industry standards committees or working groups (ISA, IEEE, IEC, or equivalent).
  • Experience with OT network and cybersecurity architecture at the physical layer, including IEC 62443 or NIST SP 800-82 as applied to instrumentation infrastructure.

title: Principal Nuclear Instrumentation & Controls Engineer – Hardware
description:
About Valar Atomics

At Valar Atomics, we're redefining what's possible in energy. Our mission is to make clean, high-temperature nuclear power scalable—unlocking abundant energy for industry, hydrogen, and next-generation manufacturing. We are a team of builders, engineers, and operators who believe nuclear energy should be fast to deploy, factory-made, and built for the real world. Our first pilot plant in Orangeville, Utah will demonstrate how advanced nuclear systems and fuel fabrication can power the future. Joining Valar Atomics means becoming part of a company where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level.

The Team 

You will be joining Valar Atomics' Instrumentation, Control & Electrical (IC&E) organization, working on the Reactor side of the program. Nuclear I&C Hardware Engineers own the instruments that measure the reactor itself neutron flux across startup, intermediate, and power ranges, core and primary loop temperatures and pressures, and radiation levels throughout the plant along with the signal chains that carry those measurements to the protection and control systems. You will work alongside I&C, electrical, reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, and nuclear safety engineers in a hands-on environment where measurement quality directly supports reactor safety. As a principal engineer, you will be among the discipline's most senior technical voices: an architect of its measurement systems, a final checker of its highest-consequence work, and a standard-setter for the engineers who will build their careers here. The team values technical depth, disciplined documentation, and a safety-first culture. 

The Role

Valar Atomics is seeking Principal Nuclear I&C Engineers to own the technical direction of nuclear instrumentation plant design for our high temperature gas-cooled reactor program. The role spans the full domain neutron flux detection, radiation monitoring, reactor protection system sensors and signal chains, and process instrumentation in nuclear service, but at the level of measurement architecture, application and qualification strategy, and design authority rather than routine design execution. The focus is the application of vendor-supplied instrumentation in plant design, not instrument or detector development. This is a principal position: you will define the reactor measurement architecture and instrumentation application strategy for a first-of-a-kind reactor, hold final technical approval within assigned domains for safety-significant instrumentation designs and qualification bases, direct the resolution of the hardest measurement application problems in the program, represent the discipline in licensing and regulatory engagements, and build the engineering capability of the organization around you. Where a Staff Engineer owns the discipline's design bases and quality, the Principal Engineer owns where the discipline is going. 

Key Responsibilities 

Measurement Architecture and Technical Strategy 

  • Define and own the reactor measurement architecture across the program: the neutron flux measurement strategy across startup, intermediate, and power ranges, the reactor protection system sensor architecture, radiation monitoring architecture, and the measurement strategy for primary-loop process variables in high-temperature helium service. 
  • Author and own the discipline's philosophy and basis documents: instrumentation design basis, signal chain design philosophy, setpoint and uncertainty methodology basis, and the environmental and radiation qualification program basis that constrain and guide all downstream instrumentation engineering. 
  • Own the instrumentation application strategy for first-of-a-kind reactor conditions: technology and vendor selection across available detector and sensor platforms, application-specific qualification strategy, standardization across the plant and future units, and supply continuity and obsolescence strategy for critical instruments. 
  • Own the discipline's standards program within assigned domains: set the framework and priorities for design bases and standards, delegate authorship to staff and senior engineers, and approve them for release; drive convergence across the program. 
  • Evaluate emerging, commercially maturing measurement technology, advanced detectors, distributed and optical sensing, digital signal processing platforms, and decide what is adopted into plant design, what is piloted, and what is excluded, balancing capability against qualification burden, licensing risk, and long-term supportability. 

Design Authority and Technical Governance 

  • Serve as a discipline design authority: hold final technical approval, within assigned domains, for safety-significant instrumentation designs, qualification bases and dispositions, deviations from design bases, and concessions; adjudicate technical disputes within the discipline and represent it in cross-discipline conflicts at program level. 
  • Own the technical integrity of reactor protection instrumentation within assigned domains: channel architecture, independence and separation (IEEE 603, IEEE 384 principles), qualification pedigree, and approval of safety-significant design changes. 
  • Lead the discipline's engagement in the highest-consequence program reviews: preliminary and critical design reviews, safety analysis and licensing reviews, qualification program reviews, and instrumentation readiness reviews for fuel load, startup testing, and power ascension milestones. 
  • Direct investigations of the most significant instrumentation problems and anomalies, spurious protection actuations, channel failures, qualification anomalies, and approve corrective action strategy, ensuring findings are institutionalized in design bases, standards, and training. 
  • Personally execute or lead engineering on the small set of measurement problems where the consequence of error or the degree of novelty warrants the discipline's most senior engineers and know which problems those are. 

External Representation and Licensing 

  • Serve as a senior instrumentation voice in the nuclear licensing effort: contribute to and defend the instrumentation content of the safety analysis and licensing basis measurement capability claims, protection system instrumentation design bases, setpoint and uncertainty methodology, and qualification arguments, and support regulatory interactions and audits. 
  • Represent Valar Atomics to strategic detector and instrumentation vendors at a senior technical level; own long-term vendor technical relationships, qualification expectations, supply continuity for critical detectors, and escalation of systemic vendor issues. 
  • Represent the company in industry and standards forums as appropriate (IEEE Nuclear Power Engineering Committee working groups, IEC SC45A, advanced reactor industry groups); bring emerging standards and regulatory developments back into program strategy before they become constraints. 

Organizational Capability 

  • Build the discipline's engineering capability: define the technical competencies the nuclear instrumentation organization needs, shape role definitions and the technical career ladder with the Director, set the hiring bar, and lead technical interviews for senior positions. 
  • Mentor staff and senior engineers toward independent technical authority; sponsor their development through delegation of ownership with oversight rather than retention of scope. 
  • Advise IC&E leadership on technical risk, resourcing, and sequencing for the instrumentation program; provide independent technical judgment on schedule and cost pressure where it intersects measurement integrity and reactor safety. 
  • Maintain disciplined engineering records consistent with nuclear quality requirements, ensuring traceability of design decisions, analyses, and test results, and setting the example for the discipline's documentation culture. 

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Nuclear, Electrical, Computer, or Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related discipline. 
  • 10+ years of experience in nuclear instrumentation, radiation detection systems, or reactor I&C, including substantial nuclear application. 
  • Demonstrated ownership of nuclear instrumentation or detection system scope across multiple significant programs, including at least one taken from concept or requirements through qualification, deployment, and initial operation. 
  • Track record of architecture-level technical leadership: defining measurement strategy, instrumentation architecture, or design bases that were adopted across a program or organization, not just a single system. 
  • Recognized technical authority in at least one deep area of the domain (for example: neutron flux instrumentation, detector physics and signal chains, environmental/radiation qualification, or protection system instrumentation), evidenced by design authority roles, published work, standards participation, or a verifiable reputation as the final technical reference. 
  • Deep, hands-on command of the full domain: detector physics and operating regimes, wide-range channel design across pulse, fluctuation, and current modes, analog signal chain engineering, qualification methodology (IEEE 323/344), and nuclear I&C standards (IEEE 603, IEEE 497, IEC 61513). 
  • Experience with formal approval or independent-review authority over safety-related or safety-significant instrumentation designs, analyses, or qualification bases. 
  • Experience directing and developing other engineers, including senior-level engineers, and reviewing and approving their work as a formal checker or design authority. 
  • Experience representing an engineering discipline to external parties — regulators, licensing bodies, standards organizations, major vendors, or client design authorities. 

Preferred Skills and Experience 

  • Professional Engineer (PE) license. 
  • Advanced degree (MS or PhD) in nuclear engineering, physics, or a related field. 
  • Direct experience with NRC licensing interactions, safety analysis instrumentation content, or defense of instrumentation design bases before a regulator. 
  • Experience defining instrumentation strategy for first-of-a-kind, advanced, or test reactors, particularly high-temperature gas-cooled or other non-LWR designs. 
  • Experience applying instrumentation in advanced, test, or first-of-a-kind reactor plant designs, including harsh-environment installations, MI cable systems, and vessel or containment penetration interfaces. 
  • Setpoint and uncertainty methodology expertise (ISA-67.04 or equivalent) at a methodology-ownership level. 
  • Participation in IEEE NPEC, IEC SC45A, or equivalent standards development. 
  • Working experience under NQA-1 / 10 CFR 50 Appendix B quality programs at a program-governance level.

description:

You will be joining Valar Atomics' Automation and Controls team within the Instrumentation, Control & Electrical (IC&E) organization. I&C Software Engineers own the logic and data layer PLC and DCS application code, ISA-88 batch sequences, SCADA and HMI applications, historian infrastructure, and enterprise integration across the reactor program and fuel manufacturing operations. You will work alongside I&C Hardware, electrical, process, and nuclear safety engineers in an environment that blends traditional control systems with modern software and data integration practice. The team values operator-focused design, data integrity, disciplined documentation, and a safety-first culture.

The Role

Valar Atomics is seeking Senior Automation and Controls Engineers to develop, configure, test, and commission the control system software for our reactor and nuclear fuel manufacturing facilities. The role covers PLC and DCS programming, SCADA and HMI application development, ISA-88 batch control, alarm management, safety logic programming, historian configuration, and ISA-95 enterprise integration supporting both capital projects and ongoing plant operations. This is a senior position: you will own controls software scope end-to-end, from functional specification through commissioning and long-term support, and provide technical direction to contractors, vendors, and junior engineers.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain PLC and DCS application programs using platforms such as Rockwell ControlLogix/CompactLogix, Siemens S7/TIA Portal, Emerson, or equivalent; program in ladder logic, function block, structured text, and sequential function chart per IEC 61131-3.
  • Develop and configure SCADA applications on platforms such as Ignition, Rockwell FactoryTalk, AVEVA System Platform, Siemens WinCC, or equivalent; build and maintain tag databases, user-defined types, communication drivers, scripting, templates, and client and redundancy architecture.
  • Design HMI displays at both the local panel level (Rockwell PanelView, Siemens WinCC, or equivalent) and the supervisory SCADA level in accordance with ISA-101 and High-Performance HMI (HPHMI) principles, including display hierarchy, navigation, and situational awareness graphics.
  • Develop batch control software in accordance with ISA-88, including phase logic, equipment modules, unit procedures, recipe management, equipment arbitration, and material tracking; build the supervisory batch layer for batch execution monitoring, unit status, and recipe progress display and reporting.
  • Configure and manage alarm system software to ISA-18.2, including setpoints, priorities, deadbands, shelving and suppression logic, and alarm performance KPI reporting.
  • Program, configure, and functionally test safety logic on SIS platforms (Rockwell GuardLogix, Siemens F-CPU, Triconex, or equivalent) in accordance with IEC 61511.
  • Configure plant historian systems (OSIsoft PI / AVEVA PI, Ignition Historian, Rockwell FactoryTalk Historian, or equivalent) including tag configuration, compression and exception settings, and asset framework modelling; build process data dashboards and operational reports.
  • Implement ISA-95 enterprise-control integration including data exchange interfaces between control systems and MES, ERP, and LIMS; develop and consume REST APIs and database interfaces.
  • Configure and troubleshoot industrial communication protocols in software including OPC-UA, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, Modbus TCP/RTU, and DeviceNet; configure server and client endpoints, tag mapping, and interfaces between SCADA and PLC, DCS, SIS, historian, and third-party systems.
  • Write SQL queries and stored procedures and Python scripts for data processing, transaction handling, report generation, and control system test automation.
  • Apply software configuration management practice including version control, change control, structured code review, controller and SCADA application backup and restore, and disaster recovery testing.
  • Define OT network architecture and configure cybersecurity controls in accordance with IEC 62443 or NIST SP 800-82, including zone and conduit design, VLAN and switch configuration, role-based access control, authentication, secure protocol configuration, and coordination of patching and application allow-listing.
  • Prepare and execute software FAT, SAT, and commissioning test plans; maintain engineering documentation including functional specifications, control narratives, cause-and-effect matrices, tag lists, alarm databases, and as-built software records.
  • Diagnose and resolve control system software faults including PLC and SCADA communication failures, logic defects, sequence stalls, historian data gaps, and application performance issues; perform root cause analysis and document corrective actions.
  • Coordinate with I&C Hardware Engineers on I/O assignment, tag naming, signal scaling, and loop commissioning to ensure control logic and field hardware are consistent.
  • Provide technical direction to contractors, consultants, and junior engineers on controls software scope; review and redline control system software deliverables to ensure compliance with project standards and nuclear quality requirements.
  • Maintain disciplined engineering records consistent with nuclear quality requirements, ensuring traceability of design decisions, software changes, and test results.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Electronic, Computer, Systems Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
  • 5+ years of controls software, PLC programming, or SCADA development experience in process industries.
  • Hands-on PLC programming experience with at least one major platform (Rockwell, Siemens, Emerson, or equivalent) using IEC 61131-3 languages.
  • Hands-on experience developing or maintaining SCADA applications on at least one major platform (Ignition, FactoryTalk, AVEVA, WinCC, or equivalent).
  • Experience designing HMI displays to ISA-101 or HPHMI principles.
  • Experience developing batch control sequences in accordance with ISA-88.
  • Experience configuring alarm management systems with working knowledge of ISA-18.2.
  • Experience configuring plant historian systems and building operational data dashboards.
  • Familiarity with ISA-95 enterprise-control integration concepts.
  • Working knowledge of OPC-UA, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, or Modbus communication protocols.
  • Ability to read and interpret P&IDs, loop diagrams, and I/O lists sufficient to develop, test, and commission control logic.
  • Working knowledge of software version control and change control practice for control system applications.
  • Working knowledge of safety logic programming and functional testing under IEC 61511.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Ignition Certified Designer, Rockwell Automation Certified Programmer, Siemens TIA Portal certification, or equivalent platform certification.
  • ISA Certified Automation Professional (CAP) or equivalent credentials.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license.
  • Experience with ISA-88 batch control implementation including recipe management and material genealogy tracking.
  • Experience developing safety logic to IEC 61511 under a formal software validation and functional test regime.
  • Experience with OSIsoft PI / AVEVA PI including PI AF asset framework configuration and PI Web API.

The Role
Valar Atomics is seeking a Controls Software Engineer to develop, configure, test, and commission the control system software for nuclear fuel manufacturing facilities. The role covers PLC and DCS programming, SCADA and HMI application development, ISA-88 batch control, alarm management, safety logic programming, historian configuration, and ISA-95 enterprise integration, supporting both capital projects and ongoing plant operations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain PLC and DCS application programs using platforms such as Rockwell ControlLogix/CompactLogix, Siemens S7/TIA Portal, Emerson, or equivalent; program in ladder logic, function block, structured text, and sequential function chart per IEC 61131-3.

Electrical Designers own the drawing packages that define the physical electrical and instrumentation installation one-lines, schematics, wiring and loop diagrams, cable and raceway layouts, panel arrangements, and installation details. The Role

  • Produce control panel and enclosure design drawings including internal layout, wiring diagrams, terminal and marshalling arrangements, nameplate schedules, and bills of material consistent with UL 508A practice.
  • Develop grounding, bonding, and lightning protection layouts including grounding grids, equipment bonding details, instrument and shield grounding, and equipotential plane details.

  • Coordinate drawing content with piping, structural, mechanical, and HVAC designers to resolve routing conflicts, clearances, and access requirements, including work within 2D and 3D plant models.
  • Support construction and commissioning teams with drawing clarifications, RFI responses, field change documentation, and punch list resolution.
  • Maintain drawing revision control and document management practices consistent with nuclear quality requirements, ensuring traceability from design change through as-built incorporation.
  • Provide checking, mentoring, and technical direction to junior designers and drafting contractors on electrical and I&C design scope.

  • Familiarity with hazardous area classification drawings and wiring methods for classified areas (NEC Article 500/505 or IEC 60079).
  • Experience performing field walkdowns, capturing redlines, and producing as-built documentation.
  • Working knowledge of control panel layout, terminal arrangement, and field wiring practice, including grounding, shielding, and signal segregation.

  • Experience with AutoCAD / AutoCAD Electrical, SmartPlant Electrical / Instrumentation (INtools), or Bentley platforms.

  • Experience with electrical installation design in nuclear, cleanroom, glovebox, or contamination-controlled environments.

  • Experience preparing arc flash studies to IEEE 1584.
  • Working knowledge of IEEE, NEMA, ANSI, CSA C22.1, and IEC 60364 electrical standards.
  • Proficiency with AutoCAD or equivalent electrical design tools.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • EIT designation or P.Eng. / P.E. registration (or equivalent), or active pursuit thereof.
  • Experience with nuclear facility electrical design and nuclear classification requirements (IEEE 384, CSA N290.7).
  • Familiarity with seismically qualified electrical equipment (IEEE 344).
  • Experience with IEC 61850 substation automation and protection communication.
  • Experience with DC systems and battery sizing (IEEE 485/1115).
  • Experience with utility interconnection studies and PPA technical interface requirements.

  • Comprehensive medical benefits

  • Free daily lunch

The role spans the full controls stack — PLC and DCS programming, SCADA and HMI development, ISA-88 batch control, safety instrumented systems, historian and enterprise integration, and field commissioning — with senior responsibility for technical leadership of complex projects, contractor oversight, and mentorship of junior engineers.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain PLC and DCS programs using platforms such as Rockwell ControlLogix/CompactLogix, Siemens S7/TIA Portal, Emerson, or equivalent; program in ladder logic, function block, structured text, and sequential function chart per IEC 61131-3.
  • Develop and configure SCADA applications on platforms such as Ignition, Rockwell FactoryTalk, Wonderware AVEVA System Platform, Siemens WinCC, or equivalent; build and maintain tag databases, communication drivers, scripting, and alarm configuration.
  • Design HMI displays at both the local panel level (Rockwell PanelView, WinCC, or equivalent) and the supervisory SCADA level in accordance with ISA-101 and High-Performance HMI (HPHMI) principles.
  • Develop batch control sequences in accordance with ISA-88; configure phase logic, unit procedures, and recipe management; monitor batch execution, unit status, and recipe progress at the supervisory layer.
  • Configure and manage alarm systems to ISA-18.2 including setpoints, priorities, suppression logic, and alarm KPI monitoring.
  • Configure and commission safety instrumented functions (SIFs) on SIS platforms (Rockwell GuardLogix, Siemens F-CPU, Triconex, or equivalent) in accordance with IEC 61511.
  • Configure plant historian systems (OSIsoft PI / AVEVA PI, Ignition Historian, Rockwell FactoryTalk Historian, or equivalent); build process data dashboards and reports; support ISA-95 enterprise-control integration including data exchange interfaces between control systems and MES, ERP, or LIMS.

  • Own instrument engineering scope including sizing and specification of field devices (transmitters, control valves, flow elements), instrument index and hook-up drawing development, and hazardous area classification for new and modified installations; review instrument specifications prepared by junior engineers and contractors.
  • Implement and configure industrial communication protocols (OPC-UA, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, Modbus TCP/RTU, DeviceNet); configure interfaces between PLCs, SCADA, historian, and third-party systems.
  • Support OT network cybersecurity hardening in accordance with IEC 62443 or NIST SP 800-82.
  • Prepare and execute control system FAT, SAT, and commissioning plans; perform loop checks, instrument calibration verification, interlock functional testing, and regulatory control loop tuning; maintain engineering documentation including functional specifications, control narratives, I/O lists, cause-and-effect matrices, tag lists, and as-built records.
  • Diagnose and resolve control system faults including PLC/SCADA communication failures, I/O faults, loop deviations, and software defects; perform root cause analysis and document corrective actions.
  • Provide technical direction to contractors and consultants on I&C scope; review and redline control system deliverables to ensure compliance with project standards and nuclear quality requirements.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Electronic, Computer, or Systems Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 5+ years of I&C or controls engineering experience in process industries, with demonstrated ownership of complex control system projects from design through commissioning.
  • Hands-on PLC programming experience with at least one major platform (Rockwell, Siemens, Emerson, or equivalent) using IEC 61131-3 languages.
  • Experience developing or maintaining SCADA applications on at least one major platform (Ignition, FactoryTalk, AVEVA, WinCC, or equivalent).
  • Experience developing batch control sequences in accordance with ISA-88.
  • Familiarity with ISA-95 enterprise-control integration concepts.
  • Experience commissioning instrumentation and tuning regulatory control loops.

  • Ability to read and interpret P&IDs, electrical drawings, and instrument data sheets.
  • Demonstrated experience specifying and sizing field instruments (transmitters, control valves, flow elements) and leading hazardous area classification and instrument index development for capital projects.

Preferred Skills and Experience
